target_stage: Landlord's appeal under Section 38 of the Delhi Rent Control Act from the CCJ-cum-ARC judgment dated 15.03.2019.
target_court: Principal District & Sessions Judge (Central), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi

IK-188721101:L72:span1.text: the said tenant Sh. Ramesh Kumar had parted with possession and sub-let and assigned the same initially to one Sh. Ghanshyam Dass and subsequently to Sh. Bhagwan Dass, who were his father and brother respectively.

IK-188721101:L73:span2.text: The current sub-lessee Bhagwant Dass was pleaded to be opening and closing the shop and dealing with the customers.

IK-188721101:L74:span3.text: it was denied that the property had been sub let by him to his brother Bhagwan Dass.

IK-188721101:L75:span4.text: his brother Bhagwan Dass was helping him in opening and closing the shop and dealing with the customers. However, it was denied that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was a sub tenant in the suit premises.

IK-188721101:L80:span5.text: Both the witnesses deposed that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was running the shop and not respondent Sh. Ramesh Kumar.

IK-188721101:L81:span6.text: Both the witnesses deposed that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was working as an employee and drawing a salary of Rs. 10,000/- per month.

IK-188721101:L81:span7.text: The fact of Sh. Bhagwan Dass operating the shop and being in possession of key thereof was admitted.

IK-188721101:L83:span8.text: Trial court held that it was only a privilege or a licence by the tenant in favour of his brother to use the premises, which licence or privilege could be terminated at the sweet will and pleasure of respondent.

IK-188721101:L84:span9.text: Further, it was the trial court's view that Bhagwan Dass was not a stranger or outsider but a family member of the respondent, therefore, sub-letting cannot be inferred.
